---
title: "How to compute features from SpikeGLX AP/LF files"
---

This guide computes electrophysiological features from a **local Neuropixels recording**
saved by SpikeGLX — an AP-band and/or LF-band `.bin` or `.cbin` file with its `.meta`
file.

This is the main entry point if you have your own Neuropixels data. For other formats see
[NWB](compute-features-nwb.qmd) and [SpikeInterface Zarr](compute-features-zarr.qmd);
the workflow below is identical in all three cases — only the calculator changes.

## Prerequisites

- ibleatools installed (see [lite vs full](../explanation/install-variants.qmd))
- An AP and/or LF SpikeGLX file, each with its `.meta` file alongside it

::: {.callout-note}
The lite install computes the `lf`, `csd` and `ap` families. The `waveforms` family needs
[DARTsort](https://github.com/cwindolf/dartsort), which ships in the `[full]` extra:

```bash
pip install -e ".[full]"
```
:::

## Compute features {#compute-features}

The published models are trained on the per-channel median over several snippets spread
through the recording, then denoised. `compute_denoised_features` builds that table from
your files:

```python
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator

calc = SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator(
    ap_file="/data/probe00/_spikeglx_ephysData_g0_t0.imec0.ap.cbin",
    lf_file="/data/probe00/_spikeglx_ephysData_g0_t0.imec0.lf.cbin",
    name="subject42_probe00",
)

df = calc.compute_denoised_features(n_snippets=5, duration_ap=5.0, duration_lf=5.0)
print(df.index.names)   # ['pid', 'channel']
```

![What a snippet becomes: the AP band, the LF band and the detected spikes of each channel turn into one row of features. The [feature list](../reference/feature-list.qmd) has every column.](../figures/raw_to_features.png){.lightbox}

The snippets are spread over the recording, away from its first and last 5 minutes. The
features come in four families: `lf`, `csd`, `ap` and `waveforms` (spike detection and
waveform shape). Every family the files you passed support is computed, and the result is
the same aggregated and denoised table as [aggregate and denoise](aggregate-and-denoise.qmd)
produces.

To compute only some families, pass `options`, for example to skip the spike features,
which need the `[full]` install and take most of the time:

```python
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import FeatureComputationOptions

options = FeatureComputationOptions(features_to_compute=["lf", "csd", "ap"])
df = calc.compute_denoised_features(n_snippets=5, duration_ap=5.0, duration_lf=5.0,
                                    options=options)
```

The published region models need all four families, so keep the default if you plan to
predict. [Tune the computation](tune-feature-computation.qmd) lists the other options, such
as `output_dir` to keep the snippet files. `n_jobs=` computes the snippets in parallel
worker processes. Every calculator can be sent to a worker except
`IBLPIDFeatureCalculator`, whose ONE client cannot, so it needs `n_jobs=1`.

Readers are opened lazily, so constructing the calculator touches no files until you ask
for data.

The table records how it was made in `df.attrs`, and pandas keeps them in a parquet file:

```python
df.attrs["snippet_windows"]   # [{'pid': ..., 't_start': ..., 'duration_ap': ..., 'duration_lf': ...}, ...]
df.attrs["features_version"]  # '2026_W42'
```

The ibleatools version and git commit of the code that computed the snippets are there
too (`ibleatools_distribution_version`, and for an editable install
`ibleatools_git_commit_hash` and `ibleatools_git_is_dirty`).

To compute a single snippet, choose the windows yourself, keep the snippet files, or work
with a recording shorter than about 10 minutes, see
[tune the computation](tune-feature-computation.qmd).

### Only one band?

Pass just the file you have. Feature families that need the missing band are dropped
automatically rather than erroring:

```python
# LF only — 'lf' and 'csd' are computable, 'ap' and 'waveforms' are not
calc = SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator(lf_file="/data/probe00.lf.cbin")
df = calc.compute_denoised_features(n_snippets=5, duration_ap=0.0, duration_lf=5.0)
```

At least one of `ap_file` / `lf_file` is required; supplying neither raises `ValueError`.

## Naming the recording

The recording **name** labels everything the calculator writes, and becomes the `pid`
level of the `(pid, channel)` table. For a SpikeGLX calculator it defaults to the AP file
stem (falling back to the LF stem, then `"probe"`). Override it when the stem is not a
useful identifier — recommended, since SpikeGLX stems are often identical across probes:

```python
calc = SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator(
    ap_file=..., lf_file=..., name="subject42_probe00"
)
```

## From recording to brain regions

The whole path from two local files to a region per channel:

```python
from ephysatlas import load_pretrained
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator

calc = SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator(
    ap_file="/data/probe00/_spikeglx_ephysData_g0_t0.imec0.ap.bin",
    lf_file="/data/probe00/_spikeglx_ephysData_g0_t0.imec0.lf.bin",
    name="subject42_probe00",
)
df = calc.compute_denoised_features(n_snippets=3, duration_ap=1.0, duration_lf=5.0)
df["outside"] = df["channel_labels"] == 3     # the one derived column the decoder needs

model = load_pretrained("int-brain-lab/ea-decoder-channel-xgboost", revision="2026_W42")
out = model.predict(df)
print(out["predicted_acronym"].value_counts())
```

A real run, on 30 seconds of AP and LF cut from IBL insertion
`00a824c0-e060-495f-9ebc-79c82fef4c67` and saved as plain SpikeGLX files (384 channels,
all four families, about three and a half minutes on a laptop CPU, most of it spike
detection). Thirty seconds is shorter than the 5-minute margins of
`compute_denoised_features`, so this run drew its three windows with the
[short-recording route](tune-feature-computation.qmd#choose-the-snippet-windows) instead:

```python
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import (
    SnippetWindow,
    compute_aggregated_features,
    get_snippet_start_times,
)

t_starts = get_snippet_start_times(30.0, n_snippets=3, snippet_duration=5.0,
                                   margin=0.0, method="linspace")   # [0, 12, 25]
df = compute_aggregated_features(calc, [SnippetWindow(t, 1.0, 5.0) for t in t_starts])
```

```text
predicted_acronym
MB           161
Isocortex     79
root          58
TH            52
HPF           31
HY             3

mean prob 0.607   mean fold_agreement 0.823
```

The published `2026_W42` aggregate of the same insertion, built from many more snippets,
gives a cleaner picture with higher confidence — see
[predict regions](predict-regions.qmd#predict). More snippets, and longer ones, make the
estimates steadier.

## Adding trajectory coordinates

Feature tables carry channel geometry (`axial_um`, `lateral_um`) out of the box. To also
get *anatomical* target coordinates, pass the planned insertion trajectory:

```python
traj_dict = {
    "x": -2243.1,      # µm, mediolateral
    "y": -1999.8,      # µm, anteroposterior
    "z": -361.0,       # µm, dorsoventral
    "depth": 4000.0,   # µm, insertion depth
    "theta": 15.0,     # degrees
    "phi": 180.0,      # degrees
}

from pathlib import Path

from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import FeatureComputationOptions

calc = SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator(
    ap_file=..., lf_file=..., traj_dict=traj_dict
)
options = FeatureComputationOptions(
    features_to_compute=["lf", "csd"],
    output_dir=Path("/data/features"),
    include_trajectory=True,
)
df = calc.compute_denoised_features(n_snippets=5, duration_ap=5.0, duration_lf=5.0,
                                    options=options)
```

This adds `x_target` / `y_target` / `z_target` to `channels.pqt`. Set
`require_trajectory=True` to raise an error when the metadata is missing, instead of
continuing without those columns.

## Probe version

`neuropixel_version` (default `1`) is forwarded to destriping, which applies
version-specific spatial filtering. Set it to `2` for NP2 probes:

```python
calc = SpikeGLXFileFeatureCalculator(ap_file=..., lf_file=..., neuropixel_version=2)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Single-shank probes only

Feature computation assumes one shank. A multi-shank recording (four-shank NP2, NP2.4)
is not rejected: the `csd` family fails with a `ZeroDivisionError` in the Cadzow denoiser, and
`cor_ratio`, the waveform features and the denoising mix the shanks without an error. See
[one shank per calculator](../explanation/feature-pipeline.qmd#one-shank-per-calculator)
for each step's behaviour and the per-shank workaround for the LF families.
:::

## If your data is an IBL probe insertion

IBL recordings are addressed by probe insertion id (`pid`) and streamed through ONE, which
needs an IBL account. `IBLPIDFeatureCalculator` is used in the same way, with the default
`n_jobs=1`, since its ONE client cannot be sent to a worker process:

```python
from one.api import ONE
from ephysatlas.feature_calculators import IBLPIDFeatureCalculator

one = ONE()
calc = IBLPIDFeatureCalculator(pid="00a824c0-e060-495f-9ebc-79c82fef4c67", one=one)
df = calc.compute_denoised_features(n_snippets=5, duration_ap=5.0, duration_lf=5.0)
```

Everything else on this page applies unchanged. The calculator also fills
`x_target` / `y_target` / `z_target` from the best trajectory Alyx holds for the
insertion: the micro-manipulator one, else the planned one, else the histology track
(`ephysatlas.feature_computation.PROVENANCE_PREFERENCE`). An insertion with none of the
three raises `ValueError`. If you only want the *published* IBL
feature tables rather than to recompute them, download them instead — see
[load channel features](load-channel-features.qmd).

## Troubleshooting

**`ValueError: At least one of ap_file or lf_file must be provided`** — the constructor
got neither file.

**`ValueError: Invalid feature sets requested`** — a name in `features_to_compute` is not
one of `lf`, `csd`, `ap`, `waveforms`.

**`ValueError: No requested feature families match the available streams`** — you asked
only for families that need a band you did not supply (e.g. `["ap"]` with only an LF file).

**A `ModuleNotFoundError` mentioning `dartsort`** — `waveforms` features need the `[full]`
extra.

**A `SEGFAULT` during computation on macOS** — a known PyTorch issue
([pytorch#132372](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/132372)). Import torch first,
before anything else in your script:

```python
import torch  # noqa: F401  — must precede the ephysatlas imports
```

Or point the dynamic loader at your environment's torch libraries:

```bash
export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/lib
```

On Apple Silicon, torch and xgboost can also crash when both are loaded in one process.
DARTsort brings torch, and the region decoder brings xgboost, so if the end-to-end
example above crashes, compute the features in one process, save `df` with
`df.to_parquet(...)`, and predict in another.

**`AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute '__wrapped__'` from
`torch/_dynamo` while computing `waveforms` (macOS)** — on macOS the waveform step hides
the MPS backend from DARTsort while it runs, and PyTorch 2.14 imported at that moment
fails. Import `torch._dynamo` at the top of your script, before computing features:

```python
import torch._dynamo  # noqa: F401  — before computing waveform features on macOS
```
